38939.e: AR stands for Appenzell Ausserrhoden. Appenzell Innerrhoden has AI and Aargau AG.
38939.m: AR is the abbreviation for Appenzell Ausserrhoden.

38940.q: How many cantons have only half a cantonal vote in popular votes?
38940.e: Obwalden, Nidwalden, Basel-Stadt, Basel-Landschaft, Appenzell Ausserrhoden and Appenzell Innerrhoden each have half a cantonal vote. They used to be called half-cantons.
38940.m: Six cantons have only half a cantonal vote.

38941.q: Which canton has the largest area?
38941.e: With just over 7,100 square kilometres, the Grisons is the largest canton. It is larger than Valais and Bern.
38941.m: The Grisons is the largest Swiss canton by area.

38942.q: Which canton has the smallest area?
38942.e: Basel-Stadt covers only about 37 square kilometres. Besides the city of Basel, only Riehen and Bettingen belong to it.
38942.m: Basel-Stadt is the smallest canton by area.

38943.q: What does every canton have, just like Switzerland as a whole?
38943.e: Every canton has its own constitution. However, it must not contradict the Federal Constitution.
38943.m: Every canton has its own constitution.

38944.q: According to the Federal Constitution, who must approve a cantonal constitution?
38944.e: Article 51 of the Federal Constitution requires the people to approve the cantonal constitution. A constitution without a popular vote would not be valid.
38944.m: A cantonal constitution needs the approval of the voters.

38945.q: What applies if cantonal law contradicts federal law?
38945.e: Article 49 of the Federal Constitution says that federal law takes precedence over conflicting cantonal law. This is called the primacy of federal law.

38947.q: Which law is the most important in a canton and stands above all others?
38947.e: The cantonal constitution is the basic law of a canton. All other cantonal laws must fit in with it.
38947.m: The cantonal constitution is a canton’s most important law.

38949.q: Who must agree if a cantonal constitution is to be changed?
38949.e: A cantonal constitution can be changed. Because it is the canton’s most important law, the people must vote on it.
38949.m: The people vote on any change to the cantonal constitution.

38950.q: What is the capital of the canton of the Grisons?
38950.e: Chur is the capital of the Grisons and is considered one of the oldest towns in Switzerland. Davos is well known, but it is not the capital.
38950.m: Chur is the capital of the Grisons.

38951.q: What is the capital of the canton of Valais called in German?
38951.e: The capital of Valais is called Sion in French and Sitten in German. It lies in the French-speaking part of the canton.
38951.m: Sion, Sitten in German, is the capital of Valais.

38952.q: What is the capital of the canton of Basel-Landschaft?
38952.e: Liestal is the capital of Basel-Landschaft. Allschwil has more inhabitants, but it is not the capital.
38952.m: Liestal is the capital of Basel-Landschaft.

38953.q: What is the capital of the canton of Nidwalden?
38953.e: Stans is the capital of Nidwalden. Sarnen is the capital of the neighbouring canton of Obwalden.
38953.m: Stans is the capital of Nidwalden.

38954.q: Which town is the capital of the canton of Ticino?
38954.e: Bellinzona is the capital of Ticino and is famous for its three castles. Lugano is the largest town in the canton.
38954.m: Bellinzona is the capital of Ticino, although Lugano is larger.

38955.q: What is the role of the cantonal government (Regierungsrat) in a canton?
38955.e: The cantonal government is the canton’s executive. It runs the administration and puts the laws into practice.
38955.m: The Regierungsrat is a canton’s government.

38956.q: How many members does a cantonal government almost always have?
38956.e: Most cantonal governments have five or seven members. An odd number prevents ties in votes.
38956.m: Cantonal governments usually have five or seven members.

38957.q: What is the cantonal government called in Geneva and Vaud?
38957.e: In French it is called “Conseil d’État”, the Council of State. Valais, Fribourg and Ticino also speak of the Council of State.
38957.m: In French-speaking Switzerland, the cantonal government is called the Council of State.

38958.q: What is the principle called by which a cantonal government defends its decisions together in public?
38958.e: Under the collegiality principle, all members support a government decision, even if they were against it. The same applies to the Federal Council.
38958.m: Under the collegiality principle, the whole government stands behind its decisions.

38959.q: Which electoral system is used to elect the cantonal government in most cantons?
38959.e: In the majority system, the people with the most votes are elected. Only a few cantons, such as Ticino, elect their government by proportional representation.
38959.m: Most cantonal governments are elected by the majority system.

38960.q: How many members does the government of the canton of Lucerne have?
38960.e: The government of the canton of Lucerne has five members. Each one heads one of the five departments.
38960.m: The Lucerne government has five members.

38961.q: What is the parliament of the canton of Zurich called?
38961.e: The Zurich parliament is called the Kantonsrat (Cantonal Council). Other cantons call their parliament the Grosser Rat or the Landrat.
38961.m: In the canton of Zurich, the parliament is called the Kantonsrat.

38962.q: What is the parliament of the canton of Basel-Landschaft called?
38962.e: In Basel-Landschaft, the cantonal parliament is called the Landrat. Uri, Glarus and Nidwalden also use this name for their parliament.
38962.m: Basel-Landschaft calls its cantonal parliament the Landrat.

38963.q: Which language is mainly spoken in the cantonal parliament of Ticino?
38963.e: Ticino is the Italian-speaking canton of Switzerland. That is why Italian is spoken in its cantonal parliament, the Gran Consiglio, too.
38963.m: In the Ticino cantonal parliament, people speak Italian.

38965.q: Which system is mostly used to elect the cantonal parliaments?
38965.e: In a proportional election, parties receive seats in proportion to their votes. That way smaller parties are represented in parliament too.
38965.m: Cantonal parliaments are mostly elected by the proportional system.

38966.e: The government draws up the budget, and parliament decides on it. In this way parliament controls the canton’s finances.
38966.m: The cantonal parliament decides on the canton’s budget.

38967.q: Which branch of state power does a cantonal parliament belong to?
38967.e: Parliament makes the laws and therefore belongs to the legislative branch. The government and the courts form the other two branches.
38967.m: The cantonal parliament is the law-making power, the legislative.

38968.q: Which language is spoken in the parliament of the canton of Jura?
38968.e: The canton of Jura is French-speaking. Its cantonal parliament is therefore simply called “Parlement” in French.
38968.m: In the parliament of the canton of Jura, people speak French.

38969.q: In which canton is a Landsgemeinde still held every year today?
38969.e: Today there is a Landsgemeinde only in Glarus and in Appenzell Innerrhoden. There, people vote in the open air.

38970.q: What form of democracy is a Landsgemeinde?
38970.e: At the Landsgemeinde, the voters gather and decide for themselves. It is the oldest form of direct democracy in Switzerland.
38970.m: The Landsgemeinde is an assembly democracy.

38971.q: How do people vote at a Landsgemeinde?
38971.e: At the Landsgemeinde, the voters stand in a ring and raise their hand, often holding their voting card.
38971.m: At the Landsgemeinde, people vote by raising their hands.

38972.q: Which tax is levied only by the cantons and municipalities, but not by the Confederation?
38972.e: Wealth tax is a matter for the cantons and municipalities. The Confederation does not tax the wealth of private individuals.
38972.m: Wealth tax is levied only by the cantons and municipalities.

38973.q: What is it called when cantons try to attract companies and residents with low taxes?
38973.e: Because each canton sets its own tax rates, the cantons compete with each other. This tax competition is a result of federalism.
38973.m: Different cantonal taxes lead to tax competition.

38974.q: What does it mean that the cantons have their own taxing power?
a: They may levy their own taxes and set the amount themselves
They do not have to collect any taxes
They may only levy dog taxes
38974.e: The cantons may levy their own taxes and decide the tax rates themselves. A federal law only harmonises the rules, not the level of the taxes.
38974.m: The cantons decide the level of their taxes themselves.

38975.q: In which canton do you pay income tax if you move house during the year?
a: In the canton you live in at the end of the year
In the canton where you were born
In the canton you lived in at the start of the year
38975.e: What counts is where you live at the end of the tax period, that is on 31 December. This canton taxes the whole year’s income.
38975.m: If you move, you pay income tax in the canton you live in at the end of the year.

38976.q: Who is responsible for inheritance tax in Switzerland?
38976.e: There is no federal inheritance tax. Each canton decides for itself whether inheritance tax is charged and how much.
38976.m: Inheritance tax is a matter for the cantons.

38977.q: Which tax may only the Confederation levy?
38977.e: According to the Federal Constitution, VAT is a federal tax. The cantons may not levy a similar tax.
38977.m: VAT is purely a federal tax.

38978.q: Who is mainly responsible for compulsory schooling in Switzerland?
38978.e: According to Article 62 of the Federal Constitution, schooling is a matter for the cantons. That is why there are differences from canton to canton.
38978.m: The cantons are responsible for state schools.

38979.q: What is the joint curriculum of the German-speaking Swiss cantons called?
38979.e: Lehrplan 21 applies in the 21 German-speaking and multilingual cantons. The cantons developed it together.

38980.q: How many years does compulsory schooling last in most cantons, including kindergarten?
38980.e: Compulsory schooling includes two years of kindergarten, six years of primary school and three years of lower secondary school. That makes eleven years.

38981.q: Since a popular vote in 1985, when does the school year begin in Switzerland?
38981.e: In 1985, the people approved a common start of the school year in late summer. Before that, the school year began in spring in several cantons.
38981.m: The school year begins in late summer throughout Switzerland.

38982.q: What is the joint curriculum of the French-speaking cantons called?
38982.e: French-speaking Switzerland has the Plan d’études romand (PER). In German-speaking Switzerland, Lehrplan 21 applies.
38982.m: French-speaking Switzerland works with the Plan d’études romand.

38983.q: Under HarmoS, at what age does compulsory schooling begin with kindergarten?
38983.e: In the HarmoS cantons, children must go to kindergarten from the age of 4. Kindergarten counts as part of compulsory schooling.
38983.m: Under HarmoS, compulsory schooling begins at 4.

38984.q: How many years does compulsory schooling last under HarmoS, counting kindergarten?
38984.e: Under HarmoS, compulsory schooling lasts 11 years: 2 years of kindergarten, 6 years of primary school and 3 years of lower secondary school.
38984.m: Under HarmoS, compulsory schooling lasts 11 years.

38985.q: Besides fixed school hours, what must HarmoS cantons offer?
38985.e: The cantons that have joined commit themselves to fixed school hours and to offering day care, for example lunch clubs and supervision. Using them is voluntary.
38985.m: HarmoS requires fixed school hours and day care facilities.

38986.q: What is the purpose of fiscal equalisation between the cantons?
a: Rich cantons and the Confederation support poorer cantons
All cantons pay the same amount to the army
The cantons share their money with municipalities abroad
The Confederation takes all taxes away from the cantons
38986.e: Fiscal equalisation makes sure that all cantons have enough money for their tasks. It was reorganised with the NFA.
38986.m: Fiscal equalisation helps financially weak cantons.

38987.q: What are cantons called that pay into fiscal equalisation?
38987.e: Financially strong cantons such as Zug or Zurich pay in and are called donor cantons. The others receive money and are called recipient cantons.
38987.m: Donor cantons pay into fiscal equalisation.

38988.q: What are cantons called that receive money from fiscal equalisation?
38988.e: Cantons with low tax revenue, for example Uri or Jura, receive money from fiscal equalisation. They are called recipient cantons.
38988.m: Recipient cantons receive money from fiscal equalisation.

38989.q: Why do some cantons have less tax revenue than others?
a: Because there are fewer companies and high earners there
Because they are not allowed to levy taxes
Because the Federal Council decides so
38989.e: Cantons with little economic strength collect less tax. The resource equalisation therefore gives them extra money.
38989.m: Economically weak cantons receive money from fiscal equalisation.

38990.q: Why do mountain cantons receive money from fiscal equalisation?
a: Roads and services in the mountains cost more
Because they are the oldest cantons
38990.e: Steep terrain, long distances and few inhabitants make many tasks more expensive. The burden equalisation compensates for these costs.
38990.m: Mountain cantons receive money for their higher costs.

38991.q: Who pays for the NFA’s resource equalisation?
38991.e: The resource equalisation is funded jointly by the Confederation and the cantons with strong resources. The Confederation pays the larger share.
38991.m: The Confederation and financially strong cantons pay for the resource equalisation.

38992.q: Which of these cantons pays into the resource equalisation?
38992.e: Zug is one of the donor cantons, as are Zurich, Geneva, Schwyz, Nidwalden and Basel-Stadt. Uri, Jura and Valais receive money.
38992.m: Zug is one of the donor cantons in fiscal equalisation.

38993.q: Which of these cantons receives money from fiscal equalisation?
38993.e: Uri has low tax revenue and receives money. Zug, Zurich and Geneva are donor cantons.
38993.m: Uri receives money from fiscal equalisation.

38994.q: Which task did the Confederation take over completely from the cantons with the NFA?
38994.e: With the NFA, building, running and maintaining the national motorways became entirely a federal task. The aim was to make responsibilities clearer.
38994.m: Since the NFA, the national motorways are purely a federal matter.

38995.q: How many stars are on the coat of arms of the canton of Valais?
38995.e: The coat of arms of Valais is divided vertically into white and red and has 13 stars. They recall the old districts of Valais.
38995.m: The coat of arms of Valais has 13 stars.

38996.q: Which motto is on the coat of arms of the canton of Vaud?
38996.e: The green and white coat of arms of Vaud bears the words “Liberté et Patrie”, meaning “Freedom and Fatherland”. The motto dates from the time the canton was founded.
38996.m: The coat of arms of Vaud bears the motto Liberté et Patrie.

38997.q: Who is represented in the Conference of Cantonal Governments (KdK)?
a: All the members of the Council of States
38997.e: Each of the 26 cantonal governments has a seat in the KdK. That way the cantons can act together.
38997.m: All the cantonal governments are represented in the KdK.

38998.q: Why do the cantons act together in the Conference of Cantonal Governments?
a: Together they carry more weight with the Confederation
Because otherwise they may not make laws
Because the Federal Council orders it
38998.e: When all 26 cantons speak with one voice, the Confederation listens to them more. That is why the cantonal governments work together in the KdK.
38998.m: Together, the cantons carry more weight with the Confederation.

38999.q: In which city is the Conference of Cantonal Governments based?
38999.e: The KdK has its secretariat in the House of the Cantons in Bern, close to the Federal Palace.
38999.m: The KdK is based in Bern.

39000.q: What is a main aim of the Conference of Cantonal Governments?
a: To represent the cantons’ interests to the Confederation
39000.e: The KdK makes sure that the cantons represent their interests to the Confederation together. It also promotes cooperation between the cantons.
39000.m: The KdK represents the cantons’ interests to the Confederation.

39001.q: How many cantonal governments are represented in the Conference of Cantonal Governments?
39001.e: Switzerland has 26 cantons. Each cantonal government has a seat in the KdK.
39001.m: All 26 cantons are represented in the KdK.

39002.q: Which conference brings together the cantonal ministers of education?
a: The Conference of Cantonal Ministers of Education (EDK)
39002.e: In the EDK, the cantons work together on schools, for example on the curriculum. There are conferences like this for many areas.
39002.m: In the EDK, the cantons work together on education.

39003.q: What is a concordat in Swiss politics?
a: A ruling of the Federal Supreme Court
39003.e: A concordat is an agreement that two or more cantons make with each other. In this way they deal with shared tasks without the Confederation.
39003.m: A concordat is a treaty between cantons.

39004.q: What must cantons bear in mind with a concordat?
a: It must not contradict federal law
It must be approved by other countries
It may only apply for one year
39004.e: Cantons may make treaties with each other. However, these must not go against federal law.
39004.m: A concordat must not contradict federal law.

39005.q: Which problem is the so-called hooligan concordat aimed at?
39005.e: The concordat on measures against violence at sports events allows, for example, bans from certain areas. It is meant to prevent riots around football and ice hockey matches.
39005.m: The hooligan concordat fights violence at sports events.

39006.q: Why do cantons make a concordat?
a: To deal with a task together
39006.e: Some tasks are hard for one canton to manage alone, for example running prisons. With a concordat, cantons work together.
39006.m: With a concordat, cantons deal with tasks together.

a: Money to support someone’s education or training
39007.e: With a grant, the canton helps people who could otherwise hardly afford education or training. The cantons have common rules for this.
39007.m: A grant helps to pay for education or training.

39008.q: Who pays part of the costs when someone goes to university in another canton?
39008.e: Universities are expensive. That is why the canton of residence pays a contribution to the university in the other canton. The cantons have an agreement on this.
39008.m: The canton of residence contributes to the cost of studying.

39009.q: Who decides whether a canton joins a concordat?
39009.e: Each canton decides on joining according to its own law, often through parliament or in a popular vote. No canton can be forced to join.
39009.m: Each canton decides for itself whether to join a concordat.

a: Member states have their own powers
39010.e: In federalism, the state as a whole and its member states share power. In Switzerland, the cantons are the member states.
39010.m: In federalism, the member states have their own powers.

39011.q: Which municipality moved from the canton of Bern to the canton of Jura on 1 January 2026?
39011.e: In 2021, the voters of Moutier decided to move to the canton of Jura. The change of canton took place on 1 January 2026.
39011.m: Moutier has belonged to the canton of Jura since 2026.

39012.q: What is cooperation between the cantons without the Confederation called?
39012.e: When cantons work directly with each other, this is called horizontal federalism. Cooperation between the Confederation and the cantons is called vertical.
39012.m: Cooperation between cantons is called horizontal federalism.

39013.q: How do people vote in cantons without a Landsgemeinde?
a: By raising hands in the ring
39013.e: Most cantons have no Landsgemeinde. There, people vote at the ballot box or by post.
39013.m: Without a Landsgemeinde, people vote at the ballot box.

39014.q: What does the Glarus Landsgemeinde decide on, among other things?
39014.e: In Glarus, the Landsgemeinde is the highest body. It decides on changes to the constitution and laws and on major spending.
39014.m: In Glarus, the Landsgemeinde passes the cantonal laws.

39015.q: How many old leagues are united in the coat of arms of the Grisons?
39015.e: The coat of arms of the Grisons unites the emblems of the Grey League, the League of God’s House and the League of the Ten Jurisdictions. The canton grew out of these three leagues.
39015.m: The coat of arms of the Grisons recalls the three old leagues.

39016.q: How is the coat of arms of the canton of Zurich divided?
39016.e: The Zurich coat of arms is divided diagonally, white at the top and blue at the bottom. You can also see these colours on Zurich’s trams.
39016.m: The Zurich coat of arms is divided diagonally into white and blue.

39017.q: Which colours does the vertically divided coat of arms of the canton of Lucerne show?
39017.e: The Lucerne coat of arms is divided vertically, blue on the left and white on the right. It is one of the simplest cantonal coats of arms.
39017.m: The Lucerne coat of arms is blue and white.

39018.q: What does the coat of arms of the canton of Zug show?
39018.e: The Zug coat of arms is white with a blue horizontal band in the middle. White and blue are the cantonal colours of Zug.
39018.m: The Zug coat of arms shows a blue band on white.

39019.q: Which canton has the most inhabitants?
39019.e: More than 1.5 million people live in the canton of Zurich (as of 2024). This makes it clearly the most populous canton.
39019.m: Zurich is the most populous canton.

39020.q: Which canton has the abbreviation SZ?
39020.e: SZ stands for Schwyz. Solothurn has SO, Schaffhausen SH and St Gallen SG.
39020.m: SZ is the abbreviation for the canton of Schwyz.

39021.q: Which of these cantons is officially bilingual in German and French?
39021.e: In the canton of Fribourg, French and German are official languages. Bern and Valais are also bilingual.

39022.q: Which town is the capital of the canton of Vaud?
39022.e: Lausanne on Lake Geneva is the capital of Vaud. The Federal Supreme Court is also based there.
39022.m: Lausanne is the capital of the canton of Vaud.

39023.q: What is the capital of the canton of Aargau?
39023.e: Aarau is the capital of Aargau. In 1798 the town was briefly the first capital of the Helvetic Republic.
39023.m: Aarau is the capital of the canton of Aargau.

39024.q: According to the Federal Constitution, what kind of constitution must every canton have?
39024.e: Article 51 of the Federal Constitution says that every canton shall have a democratic constitution. So a canton may not have a king, for example.
39024.m: Every canton must have a democratic constitution.

39025.q: What is the tax called that companies pay on their profit?
39025.e: Companies pay a profit tax on their profit to the Confederation, the canton and the municipality. The cantons set their own rates.
39025.m: Companies pay profit tax on their profit.

39026.q: A plot of land was bought for 500,000 francs and later sold for 700,000 francs. On which amount is the property gains tax calculated?
39026.e: Only the gain is taxed, that is the difference between the selling price and the purchase price: 700,000 minus 500,000 makes 200,000 francs.
39026.m: Property gains tax is calculated only on the gain.

39027.q: According to the Federal Constitution, who must approve a change to the borders between cantons?
39027.e: Changes of territory between cantons need the approval of the population and cantons concerned. In addition, the Federal Assembly must approve them.
39027.m: Cantonal borders only change with the approval of the Federal Assembly.

39028.q: Which canton clearly rejected looking into a merger of the two Basels in 2014?
39028.e: In 2014, Basel-Stadt voted in favour of looking into a merger, but Basel-Landschaft clearly rejected it. That is why the two cantons remain separate.
39028.m: In 2014, Basel-Landschaft said no to looking into a merger with Basel-Stadt.

39029.q: What is the agreement called with which many cantons are making their state schools more alike?
39029.e: With the HarmoS concordat, many cantons have brought into line things such as the school starting age and the length of the school stages.
39029.m: HarmoS makes the cantons’ state schools more alike.

39030.e: In Switzerland, the cantons are responsible for schools. HarmoS is therefore an agreement between the cantons, a so-called concordat.
39030.m: HarmoS is an agreement between the cantons.

39031.q: What does the name HarmoS stand for?
39031.e: HarmoS is short for the Intercantonal Agreement on the Harmonisation of Compulsory Schooling. It brings key features of the schools into line.
39031.m: HarmoS stands for the harmonisation of compulsory schooling.

39033.q: What is the right of municipalities to manage many of their own affairs called?
39033.e: Autonomy means self-determination. The cantons decide how much the municipalities may decide for themselves.
39033.m: Thanks to municipal autonomy, municipalities decide many things themselves.

39034.q: Who decides how much the municipalities may decide for themselves?
39034.e: Municipalities belong to a canton. Each canton decides how much autonomy its municipalities have.
39034.m: The canton decides how independent its municipalities are.

39035.q: Which municipality has been the largest in Switzerland by area since 2015?
39035.e: Since 1 January 2015, Scuol in the Lower Engadine has been the largest municipality in Switzerland by area, at around 438 km².
39035.m: Scuol in the Grisons is the largest Swiss municipality by area.

39036.q: Which municipality has the most inhabitants?
39036.e: The city of Zurich is the most populous municipality in Switzerland. It is followed by Geneva and Basel.
39036.m: Zurich is the largest Swiss municipality by population.

39037.q: What often happens to very small municipalities in Switzerland?
a: They are sold to other countries
They get their own Federal Councillor
39037.e: Small municipalities often cannot find enough people for the official posts. That is why they merge with neighbouring municipalities.
39037.m: Small municipalities often merge with their neighbours.

39038.q: Which body is the legislature in most small municipalities?
39038.e: At the municipal assembly, voters can take part in decisions directly. It is the law-making body in small and medium-sized municipalities.
39038.m: In small municipalities, the municipal assembly decides directly.

39039.q: How do people usually vote at a municipal assembly?
39039.e: The voters raise their hands, and tellers count the votes. On request, there can also be a secret vote.
39039.m: At the municipal assembly, people usually vote openly with raised hands.

a: An election of the municipal council
39040.e: In a merger, two or more municipalities join together to form a new municipality. The old municipalities no longer exist afterwards.
39040.m: In a municipal merger, several municipalities become one.

39041.q: Why is the number of municipalities in Switzerland getting smaller and smaller?
39041.e: Around 1850 there were over 3,000 municipalities; today there are about 2,100. Many municipalities have merged.
39041.m: Because of mergers, there are fewer and fewer municipalities.

39042.q: What advantage do municipalities hope to gain from a merger?
a: To do their tasks better together
39042.e: A larger municipality can often run schools, administration and roads more cheaply. It also finds people for the official posts more easily.
39042.m: Mergers are meant to make municipalities stronger.

39044.q: Apart from the municipalities, who usually also has to approve a municipal merger?
39044.e: Municipalities belong to a canton. That is why the canton usually has to approve a merger.

39045.q: What changes for the inhabitants after a municipal merger?
a: They have a joint municipal council
They lose the right to vote
They all have to move house
39045.e: After the merger there is only one municipality with one joint authority. But people still live in the same place.
39045.m: After a merger, a joint municipal council governs.

39047.q: Which problem of small municipalities is often a reason for a merger?
a: Too few people for the official posts
39047.e: Small municipalities often cannot find enough people for the municipal council and other posts. Debts or high taxes can also lead to a merger.
39047.m: A lack of candidates for official posts encourages municipal mergers.

39048.q: What is the role of the municipal council (Gemeinderat) in most small Swiss municipalities?
39048.e: In most small municipalities, the municipal council is the executive. It runs the municipality and carries out the decisions.
39048.m: In small municipalities, the municipal council is the executive.

39049.q: How many members does a municipal council usually have?
39049.e: A municipal council usually has five to nine members. Each member is responsible for particular areas.
39049.m: A municipal council usually consists of five to nine people.

39050.q: In many municipalities, what is the member who leads the municipal council called?
39050.e: One member of the municipal council is the mayor. They chair the meetings and represent the municipality to the outside world.
39050.m: The mayor leads the municipal council.

39051.q: In some cantons, which other title is used for the head of a municipality?
39051.e: The title differs from canton to canton; in Aargau, for example, it is Gemeindeammann or Stadtammann. The job is the same as that of the mayor (Gemeindepräsident).
39051.m: In some cantons, the mayor is called the Gemeindeammann.

39052.q: What is the executive of the city of Zurich called?
39052.e: In the city of Zurich, the Stadtrat (city council) is the government. There, the Gemeinderat is the parliament.
39052.m: In the city of Zurich, the Stadtrat governs.

39053.q: What is the parliament of the city of Bern called?
39053.e: In the city of Bern, the government is called the Gemeinderat. The parliament, with 80 seats, is called the Stadtrat.
39053.m: In the city of Bern, the Stadtrat is the parliament.

39054.q: How do municipal councillors in small municipalities usually do their job?
39054.e: Municipal councillors in small municipalities usually work for the municipality alongside their job. This is called the militia system. In big cities the post is full-time.
39054.m: In the militia system, citizens take on public posts alongside their job.

39055.q: Who elects the municipal council in almost all Swiss municipalities?
39055.e: The municipality’s voters elect the members of the municipal council at the ballot box or at the municipal assembly.
39055.m: The people elect their municipal council themselves.

39056.q: Which system is mostly used to elect the municipal council?
39056.e: In a majority election, the people with the most votes are elected. Some towns, such as Bern or Biel, elect their executive by proportional representation.
39056.m: Municipal councils are mostly elected by majority vote.

39057.e: The Einwohnerrat is an elected parliament of a municipality. It is the legislature and decides on important matters.
39057.m: The Einwohnerrat is a municipality’s parliament.

39058.q: What does a municipal parliament replace?
39058.e: In municipalities with a parliament, elected representatives decide instead of all voters at an assembly. This is especially practical in larger municipalities.
39058.m: A municipal parliament replaces the municipal assembly.

39059.q: In municipalities without a parliament, where do the voters decide on important matters?
39059.e: Most Swiss municipalities have no parliament. There, the voters meet at the municipal assembly and decide directly.
39059.m: Without a municipal parliament, the municipal assembly decides.

39060.q: In which canton must every municipality have a parliament?
39060.e: In the cantons of Geneva and Neuchâtel, a municipal parliament is compulsory for all municipalities. Municipal parliaments are much more common in French-speaking Switzerland than in German-speaking Switzerland.
39060.m: In Geneva, every municipality has a parliament.

39061.q: Which system is used to elect most municipal parliaments?
39061.e: In a proportional election, parties receive seats in proportion to their votes. That way smaller parties are represented too.
39061.m: Municipal parliaments are mostly elected by proportional representation.

39062.q: What is the municipal parliament called in the canton of Neuchâtel?
39062.e: In the canton of Neuchâtel, the municipal parliament is called the Conseil général. The Conseil fédéral, on the other hand, is the Federal Council, and the Conseil d’État the cantonal government.
39062.m: In Neuchâtel, the municipal parliament is called the Conseil général.

39063.q: What can voters often use against a decision of the municipal parliament?
39063.e: Many decisions of municipal parliaments are subject to the optional referendum. With enough signatures, there is a popular vote.
39063.m: With the referendum, the people have the last word in the municipality too.

39064.q: In Basel-Stadt, which parliament is also the parliament of the city of Basel?
39064.e: Basel-Stadt has no separate city parliament. The cantonal Grand Council also takes on this task for the city of Basel.
39064.m: In Basel-Stadt, the Grand Council is also the city parliament.

39065.q: What is a municipality’s tax multiplier (Steuerfuss)?
a: A percentage of the basic tax
A measure of the municipality’s area
A tax office in the cellar
39065.e: The tax multiplier states what percentage of the basic tax you pay to the municipality. The basic tax comes from the cantonal tax scale.
39065.m: The tax multiplier decides how much municipal tax you pay.

39066.q: The basic tax is 2,000 francs and the tax multiplier is 110 %. How much is the municipal tax?
39066.e: You calculate 2,000 francs times 110 %, which is 2,000 times 1.1. That makes 2,200 francs.
39066.m: The tax is the basic tax times the tax multiplier as a percentage.

39067.q: The basic tax is 3,000 francs and the tax multiplier is 95 %. How much is the municipal tax?
39067.e: You calculate 3,000 times 0.95. That makes 2,850 francs.
39067.m: A tax multiplier below 100 % gives less than the basic tax.

39068.q: A municipality raises its tax multiplier from 100 % to 120 %. By how much does the tax rise with a basic tax of 1,500 francs?
39068.e: Before, you pay 1,500 francs; afterwards, 1,500 times 1.2 makes 1,800 francs. The difference is 300 francs.
39068.m: Even a few percentage points on the tax multiplier make a lot of money.

39069.q: Who sets the tax multiplier in a municipality without a parliament?
39069.e: The voters set the tax multiplier at the municipal assembly. In municipalities with a parliament, the parliament usually does this.
39069.m: In small municipalities, the municipal assembly sets the tax multiplier.

39070.q: How often is a municipality’s tax multiplier set?
39070.e: Cantons and municipalities set their tax multiplier every year, usually together with the budget. That way they can react to their financial situation.
39070.m: The tax multiplier is set anew every year.

39071.q: Which taxes is the municipal tax multiplier mainly applied to?
39071.e: Municipalities mainly tax income and wealth. VAT and customs duties belong to the Confederation.
39071.m: Municipalities mainly tax income and wealth.

39072.q: Who is a member of a citizens’ community (Bürgergemeinde)?
a: Anyone who goes to school there
Anyone who goes on holiday there
39072.e: The members are all those who hold citizenship of this municipality. Where they live does not matter.
39072.m: Anyone who is a citizen there belongs to the citizens’ community, wherever they live.

39073.q: What is a citizens’ community not allowed to do, unlike the residents’ municipality?
39073.e: The citizens’ community has no territory of its own and no power to tax. It lives on its assets, for example from forests or property.
39073.m: Citizens’ communities have assets but no power to tax.

39076.q: Are there citizens’ communities in every canton?
39076.e: Each canton decides for itself whether there are citizens’ communities. In the canton of Zurich, for example, there are none.
39076.m: Not every canton has citizens’ communities.

39077.q: Roughly how many citizens’ communities and corporations are there in Switzerland?
39077.e: Today there are just under 1,650 citizens’ communities and corporations in Switzerland. They are organised in an umbrella association.
39077.m: Switzerland has well over a thousand citizens’ communities and corporations.

39078.q: In some cantons, what does the citizens’ community help decide on?
39078.e: In some cantons, such as Basel-Stadt or the Grisons, the citizens’ community decides who receives its citizenship.
39078.m: In some cantons, citizens’ communities decide on naturalisations.

39079.q: What is the municipality called in which all inhabitants have a say on schools, roads and taxes?
39079.e: In the residents’ municipality, or political municipality, all voters who live there have a say. In the citizens’ community, on the other hand, citizenship is what counts.
39079.m: In the residents’ municipality, the inhabitants have a say.

39080.q: What is the place of origin (Heimatort) of a Swiss citizen?
a: The municipality where you hold citizenship
The municipality where you were born
The municipality where you go on holiday
39080.e: The place of origin, or place of citizenship, is the municipality where you are a citizen. It can be the same as your place of birth or residence, but it does not have to be.
39080.m: Your place of origin is the municipality whose citizenship you hold.

39081.q: Which place is written in a Swiss passport where other countries usually enter the place of birth?
39081.e: The Swiss passport and identity card show the place of origin. This is a Swiss peculiarity.
39081.m: The Swiss passport shows the place of origin.

39082.q: Today, from whom does a child get its place of citizenship?
a: From the parent whose surname it bears
From the hospital where it was born
39082.e: A child receives the place of citizenship of the parent whose surname it bears. In the past, it was generally the father’s place of citizenship.
39082.m: The place of citizenship is passed on with the surname.

39083.q: Since 2013, what happens to the place of citizenship of a woman who marries?
a: She gets that of the municipality where the wedding takes place
39083.e: Since 1 January 2013, marriage no longer has any effect on the place of citizenship. In the past, the wife received her husband’s place of citizenship.
39083.m: Since 2013, marriage no longer changes your place of citizenship.

39084.q: Which document does the place of origin issue?
39084.e: The certificate of origin is a document that confirms citizenship. It is issued by the citizens’ community or the place of origin.
39084.m: The place of origin issues the certificate of origin.

39085.q: Can a person have more than one place of origin?
39085.e: By being naturalised in another municipality, you can gain additional places of citizenship. You then have several places of origin.
39085.m: You can have several places of origin at the same time.

39086.q: Which municipality is responsible for social assistance today?
39086.e: In the past, the place of origin had to look after poor citizens. Today, under the law on responsibility, the place of residence is responsible.
39086.m: Today, the place of residence is responsible for social assistance.

39087.q: What happens to your place of origin if your home municipality merges?
a: You become a citizen of the new municipality
You have to be naturalised again
39087.e: In a merger, the citizens automatically receive citizenship of the new municipality. Some cantons allow the old name to be added in brackets.
39087.m: After a merger, the new municipality is the place of origin.

39088.q: What is the residents’ registration office often called in large cities?
39088.e: In large cities, the residents’ registration office is often called the Personenmeldeamt. The tasks are the same.
39088.m: The Personenmeldeamt is the residents’ registration office of large cities.

39089.q: Which register does the residents’ registration office keep?
39089.e: The register of residents records everyone who lives in the municipality. The land register and the commercial register are kept by other offices.
39089.m: The residents’ registration office keeps the register of residents.

39090.q: Where does the residents’ registration office pass on foreigners’ applications for a permit?
39090.e: The residents’ registration office receives the applications and checks them. The cantonal migration office decides on the residence permit.
39090.m: The cantonal migration office decides on residence permits.

a: A plan of income and spending
39091.e: In the budget, the municipality plans its income and spending for the next year.
39091.m: The budget plans the municipality’s finances for one year.

39092.q: Who draws up the draft of the municipal budget?
a: The municipal council with the administration
39092.e: The municipal council prepares the draft with the administration. The municipal assembly or the parliament then decides on it.
39092.m: The municipal council proposes the budget.

39093.q: Who approves the budget in a municipality without a parliament?
39093.e: The voters discuss the budget at the municipal assembly and vote on it. They can also propose changes.
39093.m: The municipal assembly has the last word on the budget.

39095.q: What is the most important source of income for most municipalities?
39095.e: Municipalities get most of their income from taxes. In addition, there are fees and contributions from the canton.
39095.m: Taxes are the municipalities’ most important income.

39096.q: What is it called when a municipality spends more than it takes in?
39096.e: If spending is greater than income, there is a deficit. If income is greater than spending, there is a surplus.
39096.m: A deficit occurs when spending is greater than income.

39097.q: A municipality budgets 12 million francs of income and 12.5 million francs of spending. How big is the deficit?
39097.e: You calculate 12.5 million minus 12 million. That makes a deficit of 0.5 million francs.
39097.m: The deficit is the difference between spending and income.

39098.q: In many municipalities, which committee checks the accounts?
39098.e: The audit committee checks the budget and the accounts. It gives the municipal assembly a recommendation.
39098.m: The audit committee checks the municipality’s finances.

39099.q: In the canton of Zurich, what is the Schulpflege?
a: The authority that runs the state school
The cleaning team in the school building
39099.e: The Schulpflege is a municipality’s elected school authority. It is responsible for running and supervising the state school.
39099.m: The Schulpflege is the municipality’s state school authority.

39100.q: In the canton of Zurich, who elects the members of the Schulpflege?
39100.e: The members of the Schulpflege are elected by the municipality’s voters. Many do the job part-time.
39100.m: The Schulpflege is elected by the people.

39101.q: What does a municipality’s school authority do?
39101.e: The school authority is responsible for running and supervising the state school. Day-to-day school life is managed by the head teachers.
39101.m: The school authority supervises a municipality’s schools.

39102.q: What is a municipality called that is responsible only for schools?
39102.e: In some cantons, such as Zurich or Thurgau, there are school municipalities. They are separate municipalities just for the state school.
39102.m: A school municipality looks after the school only.

39103.q: Who decides what is learnt at state school?
39103.e: The cantons are responsible for state schools and issue the curriculum. In German-speaking Switzerland, Lehrplan 21 applies.
39103.m: The state school curriculum is a matter for the cantons.

39104.q: Who usually pays for building a new primary school?
39104.e: The municipalities are responsible for school buildings and classrooms. That is why municipal assemblies often vote on new school buildings.
39104.m: School buildings are usually built by the municipality.

39105.q: Which events does the registry office record?
a: Moving house, holidays and changing jobs
39105.e: The registry office records births, marriages, partnerships and deaths. These are called civil status events.
39105.m: The registry office records birth, marriage and death.

39106.q: In Switzerland, where do you officially report that a child has been born?
39106.e: Births are reported to the registry office and entered in the register there. Usually the hospital reports the birth.
39106.m: Births are registered at the registry office.

39107.q: How old must both people be, at least, to marry in Switzerland?
39107.e: To marry, both must be at least 18 years old. In addition, they must not be closely related.
39107.m: In Switzerland, you may marry from the age of 18.

39108.q: Since when have same-sex couples been able to marry in Switzerland?
39108.e: “Marriage for all” has applied since 1 July 2022. Before that, such couples could only enter a registered partnership.
39108.m: Marriage for all has applied in Switzerland since 2022.

39109.q: Before marriage for all, what could same-sex couples in Switzerland enter into?
39109.e: From 2007, same-sex couples could have their partnership registered. Since 2022 they have been allowed to marry.
39109.m: Before marriage for all, there was the registered partnership.

39110.q: Does every municipality in Switzerland have its own registry office?
a: No, several municipalities often share one office
No, there is only one, in Bern
Yes, every municipality even has two
39110.e: There are about 170 registry offices. One office is usually responsible for several municipalities.
39110.m: Not every municipality has its own registry office.

39111.q: In Switzerland, where must a marriage take place for it to be valid?
39111.e: Only the civil ceremony at the registry office is valid. A church wedding can be celebrated in addition.
39111.m: A valid marriage takes place at the registry office.

39112.q: If a family has one, in which booklet does the registry office add a child’s birth?
39112.e: After the birth has been registered, the parents receive a birth certificate. If the family has a family booklet, the child is added to it.
39112.m: A family’s details are recorded in the family booklet.

39113.q: What is the main job of the municipal clerk?
39113.e: The municipal clerk is the head of a political municipality’s administration. They carry the main administrative responsibility.
39113.m: The municipal clerk runs the municipality’s administration.

39114.q: In many cantons, what is the post called that corresponds to the municipal clerk at cantonal level?
39114.e: In many cantons, the state clerk heads the state chancellery. They are the counterpart of the municipal clerk.
39114.m: The state clerk heads the canton’s state chancellery.

39115.q: What is the office called that the municipal clerk runs?
39115.e: The municipal chancellery is the central office of the municipal administration. That is where the municipal council’s business comes together.
39115.m: The municipal clerk runs the municipal chancellery.

39116.q: What kind of vote does the municipal clerk usually have at municipal council meetings?
a: No right to speak at all
39116.e: The municipal clerk is not an elected member of the municipal council. They may usually take part in the discussion and give advice, but not vote.
39116.m: The municipal clerk advises the municipal council but does not vote.

39117.q: What is the municipal clerk often called in French-speaking Switzerland?
39117.e: In French-speaking Switzerland, the municipal clerk is called the secrétaire communal. The syndic, on the other hand, is the mayor.
39117.m: In French-speaking Switzerland, the municipal clerk is called the secrétaire communal.

39118.q: What is the smallest political unit in Switzerland?
39118.e: Switzerland is divided into the Confederation, the cantons and the municipalities. The municipality is the smallest of these levels and the closest to the people.
39118.m: The municipality is the smallest political unit.

39119.q: What happens in a municipal merger?
a: Two or more municipalities become one municipality
One municipality is split into two
A municipality gets a new name
39119.e: In a merger, municipalities join together. Afterwards they have a joint administration and a joint municipal council.
39119.m: In a merger, several municipalities become one.

39121.q: At what tax multiplier do you pay exactly the basic tax?
39121.e: The tax multiplier is a percentage of the basic tax. 100 % of it is exactly the basic tax.
39121.m: A tax multiplier of 100 % is exactly the basic tax.

39122.q: Where does a citizens’ community get its money from?
a: From its assets, such as forests and property
From taxes paid by all residents
39122.e: A citizens’ community may not levy taxes. It lives on income from forests, land or rented buildings.
39122.m: Citizens’ communities live on their assets, not on taxes.

39123.q: Where can Swiss citizens living abroad exercise their right to vote?
a: At their place of origin or former place of residence
39123.e: For political rights, the place of residence normally counts. People who live abroad can vote at their place of citizenship or in a municipality where they used to live.
39123.m: Swiss citizens abroad vote via their place of origin or former place of residence.

39124.q: What must men liable for military service also show when they register in a new municipality?
39124.e: Anyone liable for military or civil protection service must show their service record book when registering. That way the authorities know where the person lives.
39124.m: People liable for service show their service record book when registering.

39125.q: Which document do newcomers often bring to show where they will live?
39125.e: Registering often requires a tenancy agreement or a confirmation from the landlord. That proves the new address.
39125.m: The tenancy agreement proves your new address.

39126.q: What do Swiss citizens get back when they deregister at the residents’ registration office?
39126.e: Swiss citizens deposit their certificate of origin in the municipality where they live. When they move away, they get it back and hand it in at the new municipality.
39126.m: The certificate of origin moves with you.

39127.q: What must you do before moving away from a municipality?
39127.e: Anyone who moves away must deregister at the residents’ registration office of their old municipality. Then you register in the new municipality.
39127.m: When you move away, you deregister in your old municipality.

39128.q: What is the school authority called in many municipalities in the canton of Bern?
39128.e: In many Bernese municipalities, the authority for the state school is called the school committee. In Zurich it is called the Schulpflege.
39128.m: In the canton of Bern, the school authority is often called the school committee.

39129.q: In the canton of Zurich, who is the school management answerable to?
39129.e: In the canton of Zurich, the school management runs the school day to day. It is answerable to the Schulpflege, which has the strategic leadership.
39129.m: The school management is answerable to the Schulpflege.

39130.q: At federal level, who is the counterpart of the municipal clerk and heads the Federal Chancellery?
a: The President of the National Council
39130.e: The Federal Chancellery is the Federal Council’s staff office. It is headed by the Federal Chancellor.
39130.m: The Federal Chancellery is headed by the Federal Chancellor.

39131.q: Who employs the municipal clerk in most municipalities?
39131.e: The municipal clerk works closely with the municipal council. In most municipalities, the municipal council elects and employs them.
39131.m: The municipal council elects the municipal clerk.

39132.q: Which war came immediately before the first Federal Constitution of 1848?
39132.e: In the Sonderbund War of 1847, the liberal cantons defeated the Catholic conservative cantons. This cleared the way for a common constitution.
39132.m: After the Sonderbund War of 1847, Switzerland got its first Federal Constitution in 1848.

39133.q: What did Switzerland become through the Federal Constitution of 1848?
39133.e: Before that, the cantons were only loosely connected. From 1848 there was a federal state with its own government and parliament, but the cantons remained.
39133.m: Switzerland has been a federal state since 1848.

39134.q: What was the assembly of the cantons called that existed before 1848 instead of a parliament?
39134.e: Before 1848, the cantons sent envoys to the Diet. With the Federal Constitution of 1848, the National Council and the Council of States took its place.
39134.m: Before 1848, the cantons met at the Diet.

39135.q: On which day did the Diet declare the first Federal Constitution accepted?
39135.e: After the cantons had voted, the Diet declared the constitution accepted on 12 September 1848. That is why people speak of the Federal Constitution of 12 September 1848.
39135.m: The first Federal Constitution was declared accepted on 12 September 1848.

39136.q: Did all the cantons approve the new Federal Constitution in 1848?
a: No, a majority said yes, some said no
39136.e: 15½ cantons approved it and 6½ rejected it. Those against were mainly Catholic conservative cantons such as Uri, Schwyz and Valais.
39136.m: A majority of the cantons accepted the 1848 constitution.

39137.q: Which country served as the model for the two chambers of parliament, the National Council and the Council of States?
39137.e: Like the US Congress, Switzerland got two chambers with equal rights. The National Council represents the people, the Council of States the cantons.
39137.m: Switzerland’s two-chamber system was modelled on the USA.

39138.q: What was abolished in 1848 to make trade between the cantons easier?
39138.e: Before that, you had to pay customs duty at many cantonal borders. The Federal Constitution of 1848 abolished these internal duties.
39138.m: Since 1848 there have been no customs duties between the cantons.

39139.q: Which task did the Confederation become responsible for from 1848?
39139.e: In 1848 the Confederation was given only a few tasks, such as foreign policy, coins, and weights and measures. Schools, the police and criminal law stayed with the cantons.
39139.m: From 1848, the Confederation was in charge of coins.

39140.q: How many members did the first Federal Council, elected in November 1848, have?
39140.e: The United Federal Assembly elected the first seven Federal Councillors on 16 November 1848. This number still applies today.
39140.m: The Federal Council has had seven members since 1848.

39141.q: How many times has the Federal Constitution been completely renewed since 1848?
39141.e: A complete renewal is called a total revision. After 1848 there were total revisions in 1874 and 1999; a first attempt narrowly failed in 1872.
39141.m: The Federal Constitution was totally revised in 1874 and 1999.

39142.q: Who had to approve the new Federal Constitution in 1874?
39142.e: A new constitution needs a majority of the people and of the cantons. On 19 April 1874, both said yes.
39142.m: The total revision was accepted on 19 April 1874.

39143.q: Which new popular right did the Federal Constitution of 1874 bring?
a: Election of the Federal Council by the people
39143.e: With the optional referendum, the people could now vote on federal laws if enough signatures were collected.
39143.m: Since 1874, the people can bring laws to a vote with a referendum.

39144.q: In 1874, a referendum needed 30,000 signatures. How many does it need today?
39144.e: Since 1977, an optional referendum has needed 50,000 signatures, which must be collected within 100 days.

39145.q: In which city has the Federal Supreme Court been based since 1875?
39145.e: With the constitution of 1874, the Federal Supreme Court became a permanent court. Since 1875 it has been based in Lausanne.
39145.m: The Federal Supreme Court sits in Lausanne.

39146.q: Which punishment did the Federal Constitution of 1874 abolish?
39146.e: The constitution of 1874 banned the death penalty and corporal punishment. In 1879, however, the cantons were allowed to reintroduce it.
39146.m: The constitution of 1874 at first abolished the death penalty.

39147.q: Under the constitution of 1874, who was responsible for performing marriages?
39147.e: With civil marriage, marriage and civil status became a matter for the state. Since then, a church wedding has only been optional.
39147.m: Since 1874, people in Switzerland have married before the state.

39148.q: What is the conflict between the state and the Catholic Church that shaped the total revision of 1874 called?
39148.e: In the Kulturkampf, the liberal state tried to limit the influence of the Catholic Church. That is why the constitution contained, for example, a stricter ban on the Jesuits.
39148.m: The constitution of 1874 was written at the time of the Kulturkampf.

39149.q: Which popular right was added to the constitution of 1874 in 1891?
a: The popular initiative for a partial revision
39149.e: Since 1891, the people can demand with signatures that individual articles of the constitution be changed. The first successful initiative was accepted in 1893.
39149.m: The popular initiative for partial revisions has existed since 1891.

39150.q: Until when did the Federal Constitution of 1874 apply?
39150.e: The constitution of 1874 applied for 125 years, but parts of it were often changed. The new constitution came into force on 1 January 2000.
39150.m: The Federal Constitution of 1874 applied until the end of 1999.

39151.q: Who had to approve the new Federal Constitution in 1999?
39151.e: A new constitution needs a yes from the people and the cantons. In 1999, about 59 per cent of voters said yes.
39151.m: The new Federal Constitution was accepted by the people and the cantons in 1999.

39152.q: What was the main aim of the new Federal Constitution of 1999?
a: To organise the existing law and write it more clearly
To take Switzerland into the EU
To replace the Federal Council with a king
39152.e: With its many changes, the old constitution had become hard to follow. The new text put it in order and wrote it in modern language.
39152.m: The constitution of 1999 made the law clearer.

39153.q: What is at the very beginning of the Federal Constitution?
a: A table of contents of the laws
A list of all Federal Councillors
39153.e: The preamble is a solemn introduction. It begins with the words “In the name of Almighty God!”
39153.m: The Federal Constitution begins with a preamble.

39154.q: What does Art. 19 of the Federal Constitution guarantee all children?
39154.e: Art. 19 guarantees sufficient basic education free of charge. That is why state school costs no school fees.
39154.m: Basic education is free in Switzerland.

39155.q: What does the Federal Constitution protect with the term “dignity of living beings”?
a: Animals, plants and other living things
39155.e: The constitution requires that animals, plants and other organisms are also treated with respect, for example in genetic engineering.
39155.m: The Federal Constitution protects the dignity of living beings.

39156.q: What approval does every change to the Federal Constitution need?
a: A majority of the people and the cantons
Only a majority of the Federal Council
The approval of all the cantons
39156.e: Changes to the constitution are subject to the mandatory referendum. They need a majority of the people and a majority of the cantons.
39156.m: A change to the constitution needs a yes from the people and the cantons.

39157.q: Roughly how long did the preparatory work for the new Federal Constitution of 1999 take?
39157.e: As early as 1965, motions in parliament called for a total revision. Parliament only passed the text in 1998, and the people voted in 1999.
39157.m: The new Federal Constitution was the result of over 30 years of work.

39158.e: The preamble comes before the first article. It names the values and aims that the constitution is built on.
39158.m: The preamble is the solemn introduction to a constitution.

39159.q: According to the preamble, who adopts the Federal Constitution?
a: The Swiss people and the cantons
The Federal Supreme Court and the army
39159.e: At the end of the preamble it says that the Swiss people and the cantons adopt this constitution.
39159.m: The Swiss people and the cantons give themselves the constitution.

39160.q: How does this sentence from the preamble continue: “… that only those who use their … remain free”?
39160.e: The sentence means that freedom only stays alive if people actually use it, for example by voting.
39160.m: Only those who use their freedom remain free.

39161.q: Towards what does the preamble name a responsibility to preserve nature?
39161.e: Right after the opening words it says that the people and the cantons act in their responsibility towards creation. Creation means the whole of nature.
39161.m: The preamble speaks of responsibility towards creation.

39162.q: How does the preamble describe the living together of the different languages and cultures?
39162.e: The preamble wants Switzerland to live its diversity in unity with consideration and respect for one another.
39162.m: Switzerland lives its diversity in unity.

39163.q: Towards whom does the preamble also name a special responsibility?
39163.e: The preamble stresses the shared responsibility towards future generations. Those who act today should think about tomorrow.
39163.m: The constitution thinks of future generations.

39164.q: How does this sentence from the preamble continue: “… in a spirit of solidarity and openness towards the …”?
39164.e: The Confederation is to strengthen liberty, democracy, independence and peace, in a spirit of solidarity and openness towards the world.
39164.m: Switzerland wants to be open towards the world.

39165.q: What does the purpose article of the Federal Constitution describe?
a: What the Confederation is there for
39165.e: The purpose article (Art. 2) says which aims the Swiss Confederation has, for example freedom, security and welfare.
39165.m: The purpose article names the aims of the Swiss Confederation.

39166.q: According to the purpose article, what does the Swiss Confederation protect first?
a: The freedom and rights of the people
39166.e: Paragraph 1 says: The Swiss Confederation protects the freedom and rights of the people and safeguards the independence and security of the country.
39166.m: The Swiss Confederation protects the freedom and rights of the people.

39167.q: According to Art. 2, what does the Swiss Confederation safeguard besides the security of the country?
39167.e: The purpose article names the independence and security of the country. Neutrality is mentioned elsewhere in the constitution.
39167.m: The Swiss Confederation safeguards Switzerland’s independence and security.

39168.q: According to Art. 2, what should the Swiss Confederation promote between the different parts of the country?
39168.e: Switzerland has several languages and cultures. That is why the Confederation is to promote internal cohesion and cultural diversity.
39168.m: The Confederation promotes the country’s internal cohesion.

39169.q: According to Art. 2, what does the Swiss Confederation ensure among its citizens?
a: The greatest possible equality of opportunity
39169.e: Art. 2 calls for the greatest possible equality of opportunity. Everyone should have similar chances, for example in education.
39169.m: The Swiss Confederation ensures the most equal opportunities possible.

39170.q: According to the purpose article, what should be preserved for the long term?
39170.e: Art. 2 calls for commitment to the long-term preservation of the natural foundations of life, that is water, soil, air and biodiversity.
39170.m: Switzerland works to preserve the natural foundations of life.

39171.q: According to Art. 2, what kind of order in the world does the Swiss Confederation work for?
a: An order of the great powers
39171.e: The purpose article ends with the aim of a peaceful and just international order.
39171.m: Switzerland works for a peaceful and just world order.

39172.q: Which aim in Art. 2 means that later generations should also be able to live well?
39172.e: Development is sustainable if it meets today’s needs without destroying the chances of future generations.
39172.m: Sustainable development also thinks of the people of tomorrow.

39173.q: Which aim in Art. 2 means the good life and prosperity of everyone in the country?
39173.e: Welfare means well-being. According to Art. 2, the Confederation is to promote the common welfare.
39173.m: The Swiss Confederation promotes the common welfare.

39174.q: Where does it say that all people in Switzerland are equal before the law?
39174.e: Equality before the law is a fundamental right. It is in Article 8 of the Federal Constitution.
39174.m: Equality before the law is in the Federal Constitution.

39175.q: What is the first sentence of Art. 8 of the Federal Constitution?
a: Every person is equal before the law.
All cantons are the same size.
39175.e: The sentence means that laws apply equally to everyone. Nobody may be favoured or put at a disadvantage.
39175.m: Everyone is equal before the law.

39176.q: What does equality before the law require of the authorities?
a: Treat like cases alike and different cases differently
Deal with all cases equally fast
39176.e: Cases that are alike must be decided alike. If there are important differences, the authority may and must take them into account.
39176.m: Authorities must treat like cases alike and different cases differently.

39177.q: Which characteristic does the ban on discrimination in Art. 8 name explicitly?
39177.e: Nobody may be discriminated against because of, for example, their origin, gender, age, language, social position, way of life, beliefs or disability.
39177.m: Nobody may be discriminated against because of their language.

39178.q: According to Art. 8, what are women and men entitled to?
a: Equal pay for work of equal value
The same number of holiday days a year
39178.e: Art. 8 para. 3 requires equality between men and women, especially in the family, education and work. This includes equal pay for work of equal value.
39178.m: Women and men are entitled to equal pay for work of equal value.

39179.q: In which year did women get the right to vote and stand for election at federal level?
39179.e: On 7 February 1971, the men voted in favour of women’s suffrage at federal level. This made political equality possible.
39179.m: Since 1971, women in Switzerland have been allowed to vote and stand for election nationally.

39180.q: Whom does Art. 8 para. 4 aim to protect from disadvantage?
39180.e: According to Art. 8 para. 4, the law provides for measures to remove disadvantages faced by people with disabilities.
39180.m: The law aims to remove disadvantages faced by people with disabilities.

39181.q: What does freedom of religion and conscience allow?
39181.e: The Federal Constitution guarantees that every person may freely choose and profess their religion or beliefs.
39181.m: Every person may choose their religion freely.

39182.q: May anyone be forced to belong to a religious community?
a: No, nobody may be forced to
Yes, if their parents want it
39182.e: Art. 15 para. 4 says that nobody may be forced to join or belong to a religious community or to take part in a religious act.
39182.m: Nobody may be forced into a religion.

39183.q: Does freedom of conscience also protect people without a religion?
a: Yes, their beliefs are protected too
No, only members of a church
39183.e: Art. 15 protects religious and philosophical beliefs. People who do not believe in any god are protected too.
39183.m: Freedom of conscience also applies to people without a religion.

39187.q: Where is freedom of expression guaranteed in Switzerland?
39187.e: Freedom of expression and information is a fundamental right. It is in Article 16 of the Federal Constitution.
39187.m: Freedom of expression is in the Federal Constitution.

39188.q: According to Art. 16, what may every person do with their opinion?
a: Form, express and spread it freely
Tell it only to the state
39188.e: Art. 16 para. 2 says that every person has the right to form their opinion freely and to express and spread it without hindrance.
39188.m: Every person may form and express their opinion freely.

39189.q: Under freedom of information, where may you freely obtain information?
39189.e: Art. 16 para. 3 protects the right to receive information freely and to obtain and spread it from generally accessible sources such as newspapers or the internet.
39189.m: You may freely obtain information from generally accessible sources.

39190.q: What does Art. 17 of the Federal Constitution explicitly ban?
39190.e: Art. 17 protects the freedom of the press, radio and television and states clearly: censorship is prohibited. The state may not check reports in advance.

39191.e: Journalists do not usually have to reveal their informants. Art. 17 guarantees this editorial confidentiality.
39191.m: Editorial confidentiality protects the media’s sources.

39192.q: What does freedom of the press mean?
a: Newspapers may report freely and critically
Only the state may publish newspapers
Newspapers may only report good news
39192.e: Thanks to freedom of the press, the media may also criticise the government and the authorities. Switzerland has had it since 1848.
39192.m: Freedom of the press allows the media to report freely and critically.

39193.q: Which kind of statement can be a criminal offence despite freedom of expression?
39193.e: Anyone who knowingly spreads untrue things about a person and harms their reputation commits an offence. Freedom of expression does not protect you from the consequences of defamation.
39193.m: Freedom of expression does not allow defamation.

39194.q: Besides the press, which media does Art. 17 name explicitly?
39194.e: Art. 17 guarantees the freedom of the press, radio and television and of other forms of public broadcasting by telecommunications.
39194.m: Radio and television also enjoy media freedom.

39195.q: Besides organising and taking part, what else is part of freedom of assembly?
39195.e: Art. 22 para. 2 says that every person has the right to organise assemblies, to take part in them or to stay away from them. Nobody has to join a demonstration.
39195.m: Nobody has to take part in an assembly.

39196.q: What do you usually need for a demonstration on public ground?
a: An entry in the commercial register
39196.e: Streets and squares are used by everyone. That is why municipalities or cantons usually require a permit for demonstrations on public ground.
39196.m: Demonstrations on public ground usually need a permit.

39197.q: When may the state restrict an assembly?
a: With a legal basis and in proportion
39197.e: Under Art. 36, every restriction of a fundamental right needs a legal basis and a public interest, and it must be proportionate.
39197.m: Fundamental rights may only be restricted with a legal basis and in proportion.

a: A public gathering for a cause
A secret meeting of the government
39198.e: At a rally or demonstration, people show together and in public what they are for or against. It is protected by freedom of assembly.
39198.m: A rally is a public gathering for a cause.

39199.q: Which fundamental right protects founding a club or association?
39199.e: Art. 23 guarantees freedom of association. It protects forming associations and parties, while Art. 22 protects individual assemblies.
39199.m: Founding associations is protected by freedom of association.

39200.q: Which fundamental right allows you to take part peacefully in a demonstration?
39200.e: Freedom of assembly protects the right to gather peacefully with others, for example at a rally.
39200.m: Freedom of assembly protects peaceful gatherings.

39201.q: On which square in front of the Federal Palace in Bern are rallies often held?
39201.e: The Bundesplatz lies directly in front of the Federal Palace in Bern. Rallies there need a permit from the city of Bern.
39201.m: The Bundesplatz in Bern is a well-known place for rallies.

39203.q: What else does freedom of residence guarantee Swiss citizens?
a: To leave Switzerland and to come back
To be given a flat by the state
To have to change canton every year
To travel to any country without a passport
39203.e: Swiss citizens have the right to leave Switzerland or to enter Switzerland.
39203.m: Swiss citizens may leave Switzerland and come back again.

39204.q: Under the constitution of 1848, who did freedom of residence apply to?
39204.e: In 1848, only Christian Swiss citizens were free to settle where they wanted. Jewish Swiss citizens were excluded.
39204.m: In 1848, freedom of residence applied only to Christians.

39205.q: What does freedom of residence mean for Swiss citizens?
a: They may live in any municipality in Switzerland
They may only live in their home canton
They may travel to any country without a passport
They may build a house anywhere for free
39205.e: Freedom of residence is in Article 24 of the Federal Constitution. Swiss citizens may settle anywhere in Switzerland.
39205.m: Swiss citizens may live in any municipality in Switzerland.

39206.q: Which agreement allows EU citizens to live and work in Switzerland under certain conditions?
a: The Agreement on the Free Movement of Persons
39206.e: Art. 24 applies only to Swiss citizens. For people from the EU, the Agreement on the Free Movement of Persons has governed living and working in Switzerland since 2002.
39206.m: For EU citizens, the free movement agreement applies.

39207.q: What must you do after moving to another Swiss municipality?
a: Ask the Federal Council for permission
39207.e: You are free to settle anywhere, but you must register with the residents’ registration office of the new municipality within a certain time.
39207.m: After moving, you register with the new municipality.

39208.q: May a municipality stop a Swiss citizen from moving there because they have little money?
a: No, freedom of residence forbids that
Yes, if the municipality is rich
39208.e: In the past, municipalities could turn poor people away. Freedom of residence forbids this: every Swiss citizen may move to any municipality.
39208.m: No municipality may turn Swiss citizens away because they are poor.

39209.q: Which fundamental right allows you to open your own shop?
39209.e: Economic freedom is in Article 27 of the Federal Constitution. It allows you to choose a job freely and to run your own business.
39209.m: Economic freedom allows you to run your own business.

39210.q: According to Art. 27, what is in particular part of economic freedom?
39210.e: Economic freedom includes in particular the free choice of occupation as well as free access to private economic activity and the freedom to carry it out.
39210.m: Every person may choose their occupation freely.

39211.q: May a municipality ban a new bakery from opening just because there is already one?
a: Yes, it may always do that
Yes, if the old bakery wants it
39211.e: Economic freedom also protects competition. The state may not simply ban new businesses to protect existing ones from competition.
39211.m: The state may not simply ban new competition.

39212.q: What does economic freedom basically allow a person to do?
39212.e: Free access to private economic activity means that you may, for example, start a shop or a company.
39212.m: Economic freedom allows you to start your own business.

39213.q: Why can’t just anyone work as a doctor?
a: To protect health, a licence is needed
Because economic freedom only applies to companies
Because there are too many hospitals
Because the Federal Council chooses the doctors
39213.e: Economic freedom can be restricted if there is a public interest. That is why anyone who treats patients needs training and a licence.
39213.m: To protect health, some jobs require a licence.

39214.q: Which product has traditionally been a monopoly of the cantons in Switzerland?
39214.e: The salt monopoly is an old right of the cantons. It is an exception to economic freedom that the constitution allows.
39214.m: The salt trade is an old monopoly of the cantons.

39215.q: According to Art. 94, which principle must the Confederation and the cantons keep to?
a: The principle of a planned economy
39215.e: Art. 94 requires the Confederation and the cantons to respect the principle of economic freedom. Exceptions are only allowed if the constitution provides for them.
39215.m: The Confederation and the cantons keep to the principle of economic freedom.

39216.q: Which authority watches over free competition in Switzerland?
39216.e: The Competition Commission, COMCO for short, takes action against cartels and the abuse of market power. That way competition stays fair.
39216.m: The Competition Commission protects free competition in Switzerland.

39217.q: Where is the right to assistance in situations of need laid down in Switzerland?
39217.e: The right to assistance in situations of need is a fundamental right. It is in Article 12 of the Federal Constitution.
39217.m: The right to assistance in situations of need is in the Federal Constitution.

39218.q: According to Art. 12, who is entitled to assistance?
a: Anyone in need who cannot look after themselves
Anyone who earns less than average
39218.e: The right applies to anyone who is in need and unable to look after themselves. So first you must help yourself as far as possible.
39218.m: Help goes to those in need who cannot look after themselves.

a: The means for a decent human existence
39219.e: Art. 12 guarantees help, care and the means that are essential for a decent human existence. It is about the absolute minimum.
39219.m: Art. 12 secures the minimum for a life in dignity.

39220.q: Does the right to assistance in situations of need apply only to Swiss citizens?
a: No, to all people in Switzerland
Only to people with a job
39220.e: Art. 12 is a human right. It applies to every person who is in Switzerland, even without the right to stay.
39220.m: The right to assistance in situations of need applies to everyone in Switzerland.

39221.q: Which court recognised an unwritten right to a minimum standard of living in 1995?
39221.e: In 1995, the Federal Supreme Court recognised an unwritten fundamental right to a minimum standard of living. In the 1999 constitution it was written down as Art. 12.
39221.m: The right to a minimum standard of living was first recognised by the Federal Supreme Court.

39222.q: Who is mainly responsible for social assistance in Switzerland?
39222.e: According to Art. 115, people in need are supported by the canton where they live. Social assistance is usually paid out by the municipality of residence.
